Objects: a set of points {x1,...,xn} in R^F together with a directed k-NN graph, recomputed after every layer
Assumptions: point cloud is an unordered set, so operations must be permutation-invariant; local structure represented via a k-nearest-neighbor graph
Guarantees: formal: EdgeConv output is permutation-invariant, since max is a symmetric aggregation function; formal: EdgeConv has partial translation invariance; empirical claim only for classification/segmentation accuracy (state-of-the-art on ModelNet40, ShapeNet, S3DIS)

Objects: matrix X of N stored key patterns in R^d; query/state vectors in R^d
Assumptions: patterns lie on/near a sphere of fixed radius M for the storage-capacity theorem; patterns are randomly and independently chosen for the capacity theorem; one-step retrieval guarantees require patterns to be well separated
Guarantees: formal theorem: global energy convergence via the Concave-Convex Procedure; formal theorem: exponential storage capacity; formal theorem: retrieval error shrinks exponentially with pattern separation; formal derivation: the update rule is algebraically identical to Transformer attention; empirical: best average AUC on immune repertoire classification, strong results on MIL benchmarks

Objects: unordered set of points {P1,...,Pn} in R^m
Assumptions: input is an unordered set and the network must be invariant to permutation of points; the learned representation should be robust to rigid transformations such as rotation and translation
Guarantees: formal theorem: shared per-point transformation plus max pooling can approximate any continuous set function arbitrarily well; formal theorem: the network output is determined by a bounded critical point set; empirical only for actual classification/segmentation accuracy

Objects: a set of object vectors O = {o1,...,on} in R^m, considered pairwise
Assumptions: which object pairs are actually related is not known in advance and must be inferred; output must be invariant to the order of objects in the input set
Guarantees: no formal theorem; permutation invariance asserted as a consequence of summation, not separately derived; super-human 95.5% accuracy on CLEVR-from-pixels; 18/20 tasks solved on joint bAbI suite

Objects: a two-dimensional table X in R^(SxC), where S is the number of image patches and C is the hidden channel dimension
Assumptions: all image patches are linearly projected with the same shared projection matrix; no explicit position embeddings are used
Guarantees: no formal theorem, lemma, or proof is provided for the architecture; empirical: 87.94% top-1 validation accuracy on ImageNet when pre-trained on JFT-300M

Objects: a graph with node feature vectors from a countable space; at each layer, the multiset of a node's neighbor feature vectors
Assumptions: node input features come from a countable universe; multisets of neighbor features are of bounded size
Guarantees: formal theorem: any GNN is at most as powerful as the Weisfeiler-Lehman isomorphism test; formal theorem: sum aggregation is injective over bounded multisets, matching WL's power exactly; formal proof: mean aggregation only captures proportions, not exact counts; formal proof: max aggregation only captures presence, ignoring counts entirely; empirical: state-of-the-art or comparable accuracy on 9 graph classification benchmarks

Objects: observation set of input-output pairs; target set of unlabelled inputs
Assumptions: the model's output distribution is permutation-invariant with respect to both the observation set and the target set; the basic model assumes a factored predictive distribution over targets
Guarantees: no formal theorem; the paper explicitly disclaims the Bayesian-consistency guarantees a true Gaussian Process would have; empirical: qualitatively accurate regression on 1D curves, competitive image completion, strong one-shot classification on Omniglot

Objects: a molecule described as a set of atoms, each with a nuclear charge and a 3D position, not restricted to a fixed grid
Assumptions: the model should be invariant to rotation, translation, and atom ordering; filters must be rotationally invariant, achieved by using only interatomic distances as input to the filter-generating network
Guarantees: by construction, energy predictions are rotationally invariant and force predictions are rotationally equivariant, and the resulting force field is energy-conserving; empirically achieves state-of-the-art results on molecular energy/force benchmarks (QM9, MD17, ISO17)

Objects: a sequence of symbols (e.g. words), represented as vectors, with no graph or grid structure between them
Guarantees: no formal theorem; empirical claim only; achieves state-of-the-art BLEU scores on WMT 2014 English-to-German (28.4) and English-to-French (41.8) translation benchmarks

Objects: unordered bag of instance feature vectors X = {x1,...,xK} in R^D
Assumptions: MIL assumption: bag label positive iff at least one instance is positive; instances within a bag are independent and unordered (permutation invariance required)
Guarantees: no formal theorem; empirical claim only; comparable or superior accuracy/AUC to prior MIL methods across benchmark, MNIST-bags, and histopathology datasets
